html:
Franz Schubert was a composer born in Vienna in 1797, who wrote more than 600 songs as well as symphonies, chamber music and piano works before he died at 31.

He lived poorly, among a circle of friends who met for evenings of his music, the Schubertiads. His songs set poems by Goethe and others, with the piano as an equal partner, as in Erlkönig and the song cycles The Fair Maid of the Mill and Winter Journey. His Unfinished Symphony and his late string quintet are among the best loved works of music.

He admired Beethoven, who lived in Vienna at the same time, and was a torchbearer at his funeral. Much of his music became known only decades after his death. He links the Vienna of Mozart to the age of romanticism. See Austria.
sum: Franz Schubert was a composer born in Vienna in 1797, who wrote more than 600 songs as well as symphonies, chamber music and piano works before he died at 31.
